definition: Average fundamental frequency of vocal fold vibration. Lower or unusually stable pitch can accompany reduced laryngeal control.
Standard deviation of the fundamental frequency across the utterance. Reduced variation is associated with monotone speech (hypophonia/monopitch).
Average acoustic intensity of the voiced segments. Reduced loudness is a common early marker of hypokinetic dysarthria.
First formant frequency, largely reflecting tongue height and jaw opening during vowels.
Second formant frequency, reflecting tongue advancement. Compressed F2 range indicates reduced articulatory movement.
Third formant frequency, related to lip rounding and finer vocal tract shaping.
Number of syllables produced per second including pauses. Both slowed and accelerated rates are clinically relevant.
Syllables per second excluding pauses; isolates articulatory speed from pausing behaviour.
Cycle-to-cycle variability of the fundamental period. Elevated jitter indicates unstable vocal fold vibration.
Cycle-to-cycle variability of amplitude. Elevated shimmer relates to breathy or rough voice quality.
Harmonics-to-noise ratio: energy in harmonics versus aperiodic noise. Lower values indicate a noisier voice.
Proportion of the recording occupied by silent pauses; higher values can reflect slowed speech planning.
